clue.text: Mark men in branch with just a number

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: the men are placed inside the branch, so one word is set within the other

parts.note: a bough is a branch of a tree
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers
fair means just or even-handed

explanation.surface: Someone scratches a mark onto a tree branch among a group of men, to go with a single number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song here: the old English ballad about the fair at Scarborough, a Yorkshire seaside town. OR, other ranks, is a crossword staple for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and this traditional ballad was popularised by Simon and Garfunkel.

clue.text: Old enough to have flat in sheltered accommodation?

indicators.note: placed within, so the word for flat goes inside the accommodation

parts.note: a sty is a pig's shelter, here posing as housing for the elderly
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: Is a person elderly enough to own a flat in a retirement complex?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheltered accommodation' is British housing for older people; here it is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seventy years of age is a natural cut-off for qualifying as old.

clue.text: Troubled glower when fine is imposed

indicators.note: laid on top, so in this down clue the word for fine sits above the other piece

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or fine, with the 1 read as the letter I
read as glow-er, something that glows, an LED or light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone glares angrily when a penalty is levied on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glower' is not a scowl but a thing that glows: an LED. A1 is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed is the past tense of ail, meaning to suffer or be unwell.

clue.text: Material from Potter book I feature with article

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the chin is a facial feature
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A book about Harry Potter includes a feature together with an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' is not the boy wizard but a maker of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is fine porcelain made with bone ash, the stuff a ceramicist turns out.

clue.text: Short log being upended gets bust

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top
cut short, so the last letter of the word for log is dropped

parts.note: a diary is a daily log

explanation.surface: A short wooden log gets turned up and broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims DIARY to DIAR; 'being upended' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is slang for a police raid on a place.

clue.text: Having held onto seal, end up with one dancing

indicators.note: moving about, so the letters of the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: After holding on to a seal, one ends up dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' shuffles ENDUP and ONE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter not yet opened still has its seal intact, kept closed.

clue.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

definitions.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

parts.words: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour
parts.note: the many-headed serpent of Greek myth regrew heads when they were cut off and was slain by Heracles as one of his Twelve Labours

explanation.surface: Something restored after budget cuts is ended by the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests British politics: the Labour Party and spending cuts. In fact it is Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lernaean monster grew two heads for each one lopped off until Heracles killed it.

clue.text: After an attack countenance retreat

parts.note: the article a is a variant of an
a bout is a fit or attack of illness
countenance means face

explanation.surface: After an assault, someone allows a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'countenance' looks like a verb meaning to allow; it is the face.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a turnaround, a reversal or withdrawal from a position.

clue.text: Trot down to see country cousin?

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger or red
to neck a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: Run on down to visit a relative from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' is a political nickname for a Trotskyist, not a gentle run.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory US term for a rural working-class person, an unsophisticated rustic.

clue.text: Film star's pointless touring advanced nothing

indicators.note: going round, so the word for pointless travels around the word for advanced

parts.note: vain means futile or pointless
to lend money is to advance it, so lent means advanced
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A film star's aimless travels put money upfront for no return.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'star's' stands for 'is', a link. 'advanced' is the money sense, lent, not moved forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was the great romantic idol of silent cinema in the 1920s.

clue.text: Doctor going to space eliminating very small robot

indicators.note: getting rid of, so a letter is taken out of the word for space

parts.note: a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A doctor heading into outer space gets rid of a tiny robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small robot' fits the little droids of Star Wars; 'eliminating' signals the V taken out of the space word.
explanation.definitionFit: Droid is a science-fiction word, shortened from android, for a robot such as the little ones in Star Wars.

clue.text: Refusal or agreement to be seen with top off?

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement visibly
to top off a cake is to ice it, finishing it with a covering

explanation.surface: Someone may refuse or consent to being seen topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top off' looks like stripping, but it is the cake-making sense: to ice is to finish a cake's top.
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is informal slang for a flat no, a refusal or an unsuccessful outcome.

clue.text: Skill that has been uncovered by salesperson?

definitions.text: Skill that has been uncovered by salesperson?

indicators.note: beside, so the salesperson's word stands next to and before the rest

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesperson
art means skill or craft

indicators.note: with its covering stripped, so only the inner letters of the word been remain

explanation.surface: A sales rep turns out to have a hidden talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips B and N from 'been', leaving EE. The whole clue also defines: quick witty replies are a skill a salesperson shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick, witty retort in conversation is a talent associated with a smooth-talking sales rep.

clue.text: Young pro is OK tart with top on

parts.note: yup is a casual way of saying yes or OK
a pie is like a tart but with a pastry lid

explanation.surface: A young professional declares a tart with a lid on it acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppie is a young urban professional, the 1980s label for an affluent careerist.

clue.text: Air ace, top aviator, short of oxygen, desperately

indicators.note: frantically, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A top fighter pilot, desperately low on oxygen, is a flying ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes an O; 'desperately' rearranges the rest. 'Air' is a song and 'ace' the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the star Italian tenor, a master of operatic arias.

clue.text: 20 billion deficit presenting a very dark prospect

parts.note: the answer to 20 down is a sprayer, and a jet is something that sprays
a lack is a shortfall or deficit

explanation.surface: A twenty-billion shortfall makes the financial outlook grim.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' refers to the answer to 20 down, a sprayer; a jet sprays a stream. 'presenting a ... prospect' is linking padding around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is a deep black mineral, so something coloured like it is intensely dark.

clue.text: Hope maybe to embrace old social revolutionary's secret weapon

indicators.note: to hold within, so the comedian's first name surrounds the letter for old

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for social is read in reverse

parts.note: a social is a party

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses PARTY to YTRAP. 'Hope' is a person, the comedian Bob Hope.

clue.text: Our heartless device for throwing one out of union

indicators.note: for jumbling up, so the letters are tossed into a new order
with its centre removed, so the middle letter of our goes

explanation.surface: A device of ours for hurling something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes U from 'Our', leaving OR; 'for throwing' mixes OR with DEVICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorced woman is someone released from the marriage bond.

clue.text: As Cinderella's slipper (and her sisters!) subsequently did?

definitions.text: As Cinderella's slipper (and her sisters!) subsequently did?

parts.words: As Cinderella's slipper (and her sisters!) subsequently did?
parts.note: the glass slipper fitted Cinderella's foot, while the ugly sisters threw a tantrum on seeing it

explanation.surface: Recalling the end of the fairy tale, when the slipper is tried on.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: the slipper fitted, and the furious sisters lost their tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a fit means to fly into a rage, and the slipper literally made a good fit.

clue.text: Journalist saying something cutting

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A journalist utters a sharp, wounding remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something cutting' suggests a caustic remark, but it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, a tool for sawing through things.

clue.text: Hems about right for underwear

indicators.note: around, so the word for hems surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: to hem in is to box in, so hems means boxes

explanation.surface: Someone turns up the hems on some underwear to get them right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hems' is the verb, as in hems in, not the sewn edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers, short for boxer shorts, are loose men's undershorts.

clue.text: One dispensing with press's second request

parts.note: a prayer is an earnest request

explanation.surface: Someone does away with a journalist's further demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensing with' looks like doing without; here it is giving out spray when the nozzle is pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol or spray bottle delivers liquid as a mist when pushed.

clue.text: My daughter arranged your stuff in bags

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: put in a new order, so the letters of your are shuffled

explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns YOUR into UROY. 'bags' is old British slang for loose trousers, and 'stuff' is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ribbed cotton fabric, the cloth often used to make trousers once called bags.

clue.text: Not prepared to see star's decline, head off

indicators.note: with the first letter removed

parts.note: the sun is a star, and its setting is a sunset

clue.text: Delicacy of deep regrets you're holding back

clue.text: Be this having developed skin disorder?

definitions.text: Be this having developed skin disorder?
